lines.opening: Hello, this is Orvane Bank's digital assistant. We record this call.

lines.purpose_before_verify: I can tell you what this is about once I have confirmed your identity.
lines.no_info: I'm sorry, I can only discuss this with the person I am calling.
lines.not_talk_once: I understand. This will only take a few minutes.
lines.tp_ask: When would be a good time to reach them?
lines.tp_outside_window: I'm sorry, I can't call back at that time.
lines.tp_no_info: I'm sorry, I can only speak with them directly.
lines.tp_booked: Thank you, we will call back on {date} at {time}.
lines.wrong_number: I'm sorry to have bothered you.
lines.condolence: I'm very sorry for your loss.

lines.id_why: These questions protect your personal information.
lines.id_explain: I can only share personal details once I have confirmed who I am speaking with.
lines.id_declined: I understand. Without these answers I can't continue this call.
lines.id_repeat: Sorry, could you repeat that, please?
lines.id_wrong: I'm sorry, that does not match our records.
lines.id_failed: I'm sorry, I could not confirm your identity, so I can't continue this call.

lines.product_line: Your {name} has {amount} past due, and it is {days} days late.
lines.ask_today: Can you pay the full {amount} today?
lines.ask_today_multi: Can you pay the full amounts today?
lines.below_floor: I'm sorry, that is below the lowest amount I can accept.
lines.date_past: I'm sorry, that date has already passed.
lines.not_business_day: That day is not a business day, so the date would be {date}.
lines.after_deadline: I'm sorry, the latest date I can accept is {date}.
lines.vague_ask: Which exact day could you pay?
lines.ask_date_for_amount: On which day could you pay {amount}?
lines.clamped_note: For your {name}, the date is {date}, the latest date allowed.
lines.recorded: Thank you, your promise is recorded.
lines.sms_line: You will receive a text message confirming this promise.
lines.record_failed: I'm sorry, because of a system problem your promise could not be recorded.
lines.paid_line: Thank you for letting me know.
lines.dispute_line: I understand, and I won't take this further on this call.
lines.hardship: I'm very sorry to hear that.
lines.restructure_line: I'll connect you with our restructuring team, who can talk to you about a payment plan.
lines.human_ask_help: Is there something I can help you with first?
lines.transfer: I'm transferring you now. Please hold.
lines.anything_else: Is there anything else I can help you with?
lines.promise_change: I'm sorry, I can't change that promise on this call.

lines.transfer_failed: I'm sorry, the transfer did not go through.
lines.confirm_again: Sorry, I didn't catch that. Do you confirm, yes or no?

lines.below_floor_final: I'm sorry, I can't accept less than {amount}.
lines.no_band_line: I'm sorry, I can't discuss your {name} on this call.

assumptions: Floor (rules 5-7), applied in this order: (1) take a percentage of past_due: 10% for credit_card, 25% for personal_loan, 50% for car_loan; (2) round UP once to the next multiple of EUR 0.05, and a value already on a multiple of 0.05 stays as it is; (3) floor = max(rounded, 20.00); (4) if past_due < 20.00, floor = past_due. floor_pct takes only one number, so the per-type percentages are in 'floor_pct_by_type', which takes precedence. floor_pct = 10 is only a fallback (the credit card value). Examples: credit card 150.00 gives 15.00, raised to 20.00. Personal loan 333.33 gives 83.3325, rounded to 83.35. past_due 15.00 gives a floor of 15.00. Car loan 40.00 gives 20.00, which stays 20.00.

floor_round only allows 'up_unit' or 'nearest_unit'. The brief says round UP to the next EUR 0.05, which is neither. 'up_unit' was chosen because it keeps the direction (up), so the agent never accepts less than the brief's floor. The real step is given in 'floor_round_step' = 0.05. If the engine supports that key, it must round up to the next 0.05 and not to a whole euro (e.g. 83.3325 -> 83.35, not 84.00).

Half amount (rule 8, ladder step 2 'pct:50') = 50% of past_due, rounded UP to the next multiple of EUR 0.05 (a value already on a multiple stays the same), then max(half, clamped floor). Examples: 333.33 gives 166.665, rounded to 166.70. past_due 15.00 gives 7.50, raised to the floor of 15.00. Car loan 1000.00: the half (500.00) equals the floor (500.00).

Units: get_account reports euros with cents (amount_scale 1). create_promise takes integer cents, so promise_scale = 100 (EUR 24.70 is sent as 2470). The brief gives no rounding rule for promises, so promise_round = null. Every derived amount is already in whole cents.

Ladder (rule 16): step 1 = full past_due on today + 7 calendar days. If that day is not a business day it moves FORWARD to the next business day, and if that is after the deadline the deadline is used (rule 13). Step 2 = the half amount on the deadline. Step 3 = the floor on the deadline, late band only (the early band has attempts = 2, so it stops after step 2).
The opening question ('full past_due today') is not a ladder step (rule 15), so opening_is_attempt = false. Attempts are 2 (early) and 3 (late), copied from the table.

Rule 17: before each step, compare it with every earlier proposal, the opening question included. If it has the same amount on the same date, skip it silently. The skipped step still uses up one step of the limit (rule 18). Hence skip_duplicate_offers = true.

Rule 19: once the customer says the full amount is too much, every later step that names the full past_due is skipped, and it still counts toward the limit. The allowed values are only 'attempt_1' and 'asked_date'. 'attempt_1' was chosen because, as in the brief, the 'too much' reply uses up step 1 (the full-amount step). Correct behaviour per the brief: never name the full past_due again after 'too much'. If step 1 is still pending, it is skipped and counts. The next proposal is step 2 (the half amount on the deadline), then step 3 (the floor on the deadline, late band only).

Rule 20: an amount the customer names from the floor up to past_due (both included), on an allowed date, is accepted and uses no step. Below the floor, the floor on that date is offered once, and refusing that offer counts as a flat refusal of the current step.

Early-band deadline = the 10th business day after today, not counting today. Late-band deadline = the earlier of the 5th business day after today and the last business day of the current calendar month. The month cap applies even when it makes the deadline today (roll_if_not_after_today = false).

deadline_adjust = next_business_day, per rule 13. A promise date must be today or later, a business day, and not after the deadline (rule 12). If the customer names a date after the deadline, the deadline is offered (rule 14).

Someone else answering (rule 2): the agent says nothing about the account and closes as not_reached/unclear. The API has no schedule_callback tool, so no callback is ever booked: callback.days = [] and tool_bodies.schedule_callback = {} (no fields exist to map). callback.max_asks = 1 and is never used. The callback, no_callback, wrong_number and deceased events all map to not_reached/unclear.

Identity: date of birth first, then postcode, one verify_identity call each. The date is sent as %Y-%m-%d and the postcode in capitals with no spaces. The brief gives no postcode length, so length is left out. Two wrong answers in total end the check (not_verified/failed). A refusal closes as not_verified/declined. An unreadable answer comes back with ok = false and does not count. The API has no hint field, so hints = {}.

Defaults used where the brief is silent: confirm.max_asks = 2, purpose_is_decline = true, after_promise.ask_anything_else = true, max_not_talk = 2, date_rules.next_weekday = 'following_week'. The brief does not say how to change a recorded promise, so the agent says it can't be changed on this call.

Hardship (rule 29): one sentence of sympathy, no ladder step and no transfer. The call closes as no_promise/hardship with add_note 'hardship'. transfer_support has no queue and works the same as hardship.

Transfers: a payment-plan request goes to queue 'restructuring' and closes as transferred/restructuring. A request for a human goes to queue 'general' and closes as transferred/human. No note on a transfer. human.ask_first = false because the brief says to transfer directly.

Notes (rule 31): one note per product, before close_call, only after the debt was stated and only when there is no promise. The reason is refused, hardship or dispute, or paid for 'already paid'. No note on a transfer or on service_error (rules 25 and 32).
If create_promise fails (an error or ok = false), retry exactly once with the same values. If it fails again, say it could not be recorded and close as no_promise/service_error with no note.
Opening: the brief requires saying the call is recorded, so the line uses the active form 'We record this call.'
The read-back question is the brief's exact wording, 'Do you confirm?'. The brief's text-message sentence is said after a recorded promise.
The brief calls the minimum acceptable amount the 'floor', so floor_names uses 'floor'.
The brief covers days_late 1 to 90 and gives no rule for values outside that range, so bands_outside = null.
close_call sends a reason for every outcome except promise and paid (reason '').
